newsitem.title: USA: Run-off set for V.I. delegate to congress.
newsitem.headline: Run-off set for V.I. delegate to congress.

text.p: A run-off election will be needed to select the U.S. Virgin Islands' delegate to the U.S. Congress after the winner failed to reach 50 percent plus one, officials said on Wednesday.

Donna Christian Green, a physician and Democrat, got 11,299 votes to lead incumbent Victor Frazer, an independent, with 10,106 votes, election officials said. The run-off election between Green and Frazer will be held on Nov. 19.
Lt. Gov. Kenneth Mapp, a Republican, ran a distant third, receiving 8,063 votes.
The U.S. Virgin Islands, a territory of the United States, has one non-voting delegate to Congress.
